Question: Was lawman Tom Horn actually innocent of the charges that led to his hanging in 1903?
Answer: The case of Tom Horn is controversial. On 20th November 1903, he was executed after being convicted of the murder of Willie Nickell. Even then, there was some doubt as to Horn's guilt. However, a deputy marshal called Joe Lefors claimed he extracted a confession - January 1902. During the interrogation, Tom Horn was still under the influence of alcohol but Lefors was satisfied enough to secure an arrest. During his trial, Horn maintained his innocence throughout. Some historians believe there was no physical evidence to link him to the crime. However, he was known for having strong tendencies toward committing violence and this had led to several arrests. In all likelihood, the facts will probably never be known. Thanks for reading.
